title: WPT task (the content of a depot item of kind task: what the task asks, its starting files and its check; docs/training.md)

instructions.description: what the model is asked to do, in full: the user message that starts every attempt, unless it opens with terse

terse.description: the same request in one line (no line break: tasks.py refuses one), for the measure of terse against full requests: an attempt may open with it instead of instructions (docs/training.md, "Tasks")

image.description: the image the attempt's container runs: a folder name in data/images/

max_tokens.description: tokens the model writes in one attempt, over every turn

command_seconds.description: how long one tool call may run in the container

container.description: sizes of the attempt's and the check's containers above the defaults (tasks.py SIZES; a smaller value leaves the default); 2 x disk + 1024 MiB must stay below memory

memory.description: MiB of memory, files in /work and /tmp included

disk.description: MiB that /work and /tmp may each hold

processes.description: processes and threads running at once

needs.description: the tools the task cannot be done without; each entry lists the variants of one need, and every attempt is offered exactly one of them (docs/training.md, "Tools")

answered_by.description: the looking tools (read, bash, a declared tool marked looks) that can answer what the task leaves open, through which an attempt opens the files of answered_in before it asks the user (wpt_check.asked_last); required with replies

answered_in.description: glob patterns of the paths under /work where the task's answers live: an attempt asks the user only after it opened, through answered_by, every starting file they match; a question counts at once when they match none (the answer is absent; wpt_check.asked_last); required with replies

replies.description: the user's replies, written in advance, to the ask tool, which only a task with replies offers: the first reply whose pattern matches the question is given

pattern.description: a Python regular expression, searched for anywhere in the question

tools.description: tools the task offers beyond read, write, edit, bash and ask, each answered by a program in the image

tool_files.description: paths under files/ (a file, or a folder and everything in it) that go to the tools' programs instead of /work: the model's own tools cannot read them

absent.description: absolute folders of the image, outside /work and /tmp, that the attempts' containers show empty: the task removes what the image installs there (docs/training.md, "Tasks")

area.description: glob patterns of the paths under /work an attempt may change, [] for none: a changed path outside them breaks the within_area part (docs/training.md, "Rewards"); a task without an area gets no such part

gates.description: the parts (the check's, or within_area) that must be 1: when one is below 1, or missing, the attempt scores 0 whatever the rest (docs/training.md, "Rewards")

repository.description: the Git repository the task works in: the agent harness fetches it at this commit when the task runs

address.description: where the repository is fetched from

commit.description: the full id of the commit

task.description: what the task asks and how an attempt runs

files.description: the starting files, by their path under files/

check.description: the program run after the attempt, which prints a score from 0 to 1

variant.description: one way to meet a need: a tool's name, or tools offered together and the paths under files/ that go to the tools' programs, as tool_files, in an attempt offered this variant only

description.description: what the model reads about the tool

parameters.description: the JSON Schema of the call's arguments

program.description: the absolute path, in the image, of the program that answers a call

names.description: other names an attempt may offer the tool under

looks.description: whether a call of the tool looks at sources, as read does (search, fetch, a file search); answered_by names only looking tools (docs/training.md, "The check library")

mode.description: a file, an executable file, or a symbolic link

content.description: the file's bytes in base64; a link's target
